validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by THREE independent origins that all name this pipeline specifically: (1) Xcel Energy's own Colorado PUC rate-case exhibit (Hearing Exhibit 106, Attachment JHZ-4, Proceeding 22AL-___G, 'Reliability - Capacity Project Descriptions'), which lists 'Tungsten to Blackhawk Pipeline Reinforcement' as project #1 and gives a full engineering/cost writeup for 'The 8" (6") Tungsten to Bobtail Mainline Project'; (2) the Boulder Daily Camera (independent newspaper, July 9 2019), reporting Boulder County's approval of Xcel's construction permit and naming 'the Tungsten site in Boulder County and the Bobtail site in Black Hawk'; (3) Pipeline & Gas Journal's industry-wide 'Planned Projects' compilation (Oct 2018 issue, Xcel data as of 8/17), which carries a standalone 'Tungsten to Bobtail Pipeline' entry (15 miles, Boulder County CO - Black Hawk CO). A fourth lead, a Mountain-Ear article on construction resuming after a COVID-19 pause (Apr 2020), corroborates via Wayback (themtnear.com direct fetch 403'd; Wayback capture 20201217015517 verified OK) but is substantively an Xcel-authored press notice republished by the paper, so it is not counted as a fully independent 4th origin. No trace of this pipeline is GEM-derived -- all leads pre-date or are contemporaneous with GEM's own coverage. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating natural-gas pipeline. Caveat for the record: this is a utility high-pressure (1,000 psig MAOP) SYSTEM-REINFORCEMENT main built by Xcel Energy to interconnect its existing Louisville-to-Rollins-Pass HP main (via a new takeoff and the rebuilt Dory Hill Regulator Station) to the existing Central City-to-Dory Hill 6" line at the Bobtail Regulator Station near Black Hawk -- i.e. it feeds local distribution taps in Boulder/Gilpin counties rather than functioning as an interstate FERC-jurisdictional trunk. That register matches other small utility mains GEM already tracks in this same batch (e.g. Doosan Bobcat, Traill County), so no reclassification is recommended, but a reviewer should read 'transmission' loosely here -- it is a utility HP main, not gathering/distribution service pipe, and not a FERC pipeline either. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster -- no other row shares this geography (Boulder County / Gilpin County / Black Hawk / Louisville, CO) or these place-derived names (Tungsten, Bobtail, Dory Hill); P0386 Taproot Baja is a different, unrelated Xcel CO project and does not appear anywhere in the Attachment JHZ-4 exhibit (which lists ~24 other Xcel CO capital projects by name, none matching any roster row). No duplicate/relabel concern.
